claims.claim: The problem has an exact objective-preserving Local Neighborhood Test Cover reformulation: after adjoining a dummy element, admissible tests are nonempty subsets of a host's closed neighborhood, and every pair of elements must be separated. Approximation and inapproximability results transfer in both directions without loss.
claims.evidence: A bug hosted at z with monitored set M is exactly a host-labelled test M⊆N[z]. With the dummy element in no test, separation from the dummy is equivalent to a nonempty signature, while separation of two vertices is equivalent to distinct signatures. The inverse map hosts and tunes one bug for each test. Both maps preserve cost exactly; empty or duplicate tests are redundant, and each certificate has polynomial encoding length in the implicit graph representation.
claims.witness: The mutually inverse maps are b=(z,M) ↦ test (z,M), and test (z,M) ↦ a bug hosted at z and tuned to M, with the dummy assigned the empty incidence vector.
claims.search_method: First-principles comparison with the source definitions and verification of both reduction directions, feasibility, encoding, and objective preservation.

claims.claim: Fixed-placement feasibility has an exact matching characterization, yielding an XP exact algorithm parameterized by the number k of bugs.
claims.evidence: For fixed bug identities and hosts, a vertex can receive precisely the nonempty subsets of its audible-bug set A(v). Thus distinct feasible signatures are exactly a matching saturating all vertices in the stated bipartite graph. Conversely, a saturating matching defines legal monitored sets coordinate by coordinate. Enumerating host multisets for each size at most k and solving these matching instances takes f(k)n^{k+O(1)}, which is XP and decides OPT≤k exactly.
claims.witness: A matching edge v-S assigns signature S to v; conversely, the collection of pairwise-distinct signatures in any feasible placement supplies the saturating matching.
claims.search_method: Direct bijection between signature assignments and matchings, followed by parameterized enumeration and running-time analysis.

claims.claim: Regional information bound: for every X⊆V, at least ceil(log2(|X|+1)) bugs must be hosted in N[X]. Moreover, the optimum is additive over connected components.
claims.evidence: Every bug appearing in a signature of X is hosted in N[X]. If h bugs are hosted there, X has at most 2^h−1 distinct nonempty signatures, so h≥ceil(log2(|X|+1)). Restricting a global solution to a component preserves its nonempty distinct codes. Conversely, component solutions combine after globally relabelling their bug sets disjointly; nonempty subsets of disjoint bug sets cannot coincide. This proves exact additivity.
claims.witness: The counting injection is X into the nonempty subsets of the h locally hosted bugs. The two componentwise restriction/union operations witness both inequalities for OPT.
claims.search_method: Regional subset counting and two-direction component decomposition from the source model.

claims.claim: If every connected component C has a universal safe house, then OPT is exactly sum_C ceil(log2(|C|+1)), computable in polynomial time.
claims.evidence: The regional bound with X=C gives the stated lower bound. If u is universal, k=ceil(log2(|C|+1)) cohosted bugs at u are audible everywhere, and the |C| vertices can be assigned distinct nonempty k-bit signatures. Component additivity gives the sum, while components and universal vertices are polynomial-time detectable.
claims.witness: Place k bugs at the universal vertex and inject the vertices of C into the 2^k−1 nonempty subsets of those bugs.
claims.search_method: Matched the information lower bound to an explicit universal-host construction and checked component aggregation.

claims.claim: Incidence-capacity lower bound: if rho=max_v |N[v]| and a solution has k bugs, then L(n,k)≤k rho, where L(n,k) is the minimum total cardinality of n distinct nonempty subsets of a k-element set.
claims.evidence: Double counting vertex-bug incidences gives Σ_v|S(v)|=Σ_b|M(b)|. Each M(b) lies within one closed neighborhood and hence has size at most rho, yielding the upper bound k rho. Since the n signatures are distinct and nonempty, their total size is at least L(n,k). Selecting subsets by increasing cardinality proves the supplied formula for L and the corollary L(n,k)≥2n−k.
claims.witness: The same incidence set {(v,b): b∈S(v)} is counted once by vertices and once by bugs.
claims.search_method: Exact incidence double count and extremal ordering of Boolean-lattice levels.

claims.claim: The problem is exactly solvable on interval graphs of maximum degree at most two. For every connected component C of order n, OPT(C)=floor(n/2)+1; componentwise summation gives the general answer.
claims.evidence: A connected graph of maximum degree two is a path or cycle. The minimum-right-endpoint argument excludes induced cycles of length at least four in an interval graph, leaving paths and K3. For P_n, 2n−k≤Σ_v|S(v)|≤3k gives k≥ceil(n/2). If n=2t and k=t, equality forces every bug to cover a full three-vertex neighborhood, every bug to occur as a singleton code, and all remaining codes to be pairs. Hosts must consequently be distinct, internal, and nonadjacent, but P_{2t} has only t−1 mutually nonadjacent internal vertices. Hence k≥t+1. Alternating hosts give the claimed upper bounds; K3 needs two bugs. Exact enumeration additionally confirmed P_1 through P_14 and K3.
claims.witness: For P_{2t+1}, host bugs at all odd vertices, assigning singleton codes to hosts and adjacent pairs to intervening vertices. For P_{2t}, add a bug at the last vertex. For K3, put two bugs at any universal vertex.
claims.search_method: Structural classification, incidence equality-case analysis, explicit constructions, and exhaustive fixed-placement matching as a counterexample screen.

claims.claim: Running the source greedy algorithm in both timeline directions and taking the better result is not exact, even on a connected symmetric instance: both runs use seven bugs while OPT=6.
claims.evidence: Exact rational reconstruction gives the forward additions (1,2),(2,3),(4,6),(6,7),(9,11),(11,13),(13,13); reflection gives the identical seven-addition trace. The six stated hosted bugs and all thirteen codes are legal and distinct. For X={L1,L2,L3,L4}, N[X] is exactly {L1,...,L6}; the reflected region has the disjoint neighborhood {R1,...,R6}. Each four-vertex region needs at least three hosted bugs, proving OPT≥6. Exhaustive placement/matching search independently returned OPT=6.
claims.witness: Hosts L2,L3,L5,R5,R3,R2 with the listed left, right, and bridge codes provide the six-bug upper bound; the two disjoint four-vertex regional bounds provide the matching lower bound.
claims.search_method: Fraction-exact endpoint ordering, direct execution of the source lexicographic procedure, independent matching feasibility, code validation, regional checks, and exhaustive optimization.

claims.claim: There is a connected ten-interval instance on which the source greedy algorithm uses five bugs in each timeline direction while OPT=4; thus the bidirectional variant has approximation ratio at least 5/4.
claims.evidence: The ten exact intervals form one connected component. Bugs hosted at I2,I5,I9,I9 realize the ten stated distinct legal masks, while 2^3−1<10 proves OPT≥4; exhaustive matching search also returns OPT=4. Direct source-procedure execution reproduces forward feasibility F,F,T,F,T,T,F,T,T,F and additions (1,3),(2,5),(4,9),(7,10),(10,10). It reproduces reverse feasibility F,F,T,F,T,T,T,F,T,F and additions (1,5),(2,5),(4,7),(8,10),(10,10). The supplied Hall-deficient sets and matching masks were checked exactly.
claims.witness: The legal masks (1,3,2,14,5,10,12,8,6,4) for hosts I2,I5,I9,I9 certify cost four; the exact two traces certify bidirectional cost five and ratio 5/4.
claims.search_method: Exact interval intersections, connectivity, explicit-code verification, Hall-union checks, source lexicographic simulation, independent bipartite matching, and exhaustive host-multiset search.

claims.claim: For every t≥1 there is an interval instance with OPT=4t on which both timeline directions use 5t bugs; consequently 5/4 is an asymptotic lower bound for the bidirectional greedy approximation ratio.
claims.evidence: Translated copies can be separated so that they are distinct connected components and occur consecutively in either timeline order. Component additivity gives OPT=4t. Earlier-component bugs are inaudible in the active copy, and every current signature is a nonempty subset of fresh bug identities, so it cannot collide with an earlier-component signature. Thus each copy repeats the corresponding five-addition trace independently in both directions. The checker directly reproduced (5t,5t,4t) for t=1,...,6; the disjoint-identity argument proves the statement for every t.
claims.witness: Take t copies of the verified ten-interval instance translated by mutually separated offsets. Their costs add to 4t, while each forward or reflected execution makes five additions per copy.
claims.search_method: General componentwise induction, supplemented by exact source-procedure executions on multiple translated-copy instances.

target_evidence: The exact source target requires either a polynomial-time approximation ratio strictly below 2 for all interval instances or an appropriate matching inapproximability theorem. The draft explicitly supplies neither, so it does not fully resolve the target. Its exact reformulation, XP characterization, structural bounds, solved subclasses, and asymptotic 5/4 obstruction for the bidirectional source heuristic are nevertheless correct and material partial progress. The parent's PARTIAL label is therefore accurate and not overstated.
